text:
Sixty-five minutes, 51 shots on goal, nine power plays, and nobody scored. Joel Hofer stopped all 29 Utah shots, Karel Vejmelka stopped all 22 from St. Louis, and the Blues won a 1-0 game that needed eight rounds of a shootout to settle.

This was not a dull 0-0. Utah owned the first period, 1.18 to 0.39 in expected goals (the quality of each team's chances), and Jack McBain had a 41% look that Hofer took away. St. Louis came back stronger late: the Blues won the third 1.11 to 0.59, and Vejmelka's biggest save came there, on a Pavel Buchnevich chance worth 35%. Across the night the chances were nearly even, 3.02 to 2.90 for Utah, and our replays of every shot split it 52-48. The Blues went 0 for 5 on the power play despite 0.91 expected goals with the man advantage; Utah went 0 for 4.

Both goalies were worth close to three goals above expected, which is about as good as a single night in net gets. For Hofer it lands in an interesting week. Jordan Binnington has been the most written-about Blue of the last two weeks, nearly all of it trade talk, and Hofer is the one wearing the shutout. He was named first star.

The shootout went the distance. Vincent Trocheck and Jake Neighbours scored in the first round, then 10 straight shooters were stopped. Michael Carcone and Jimmy Snuggerud traded goals in the seventh, Barrett Hayton was stopped in the eighth, and Connor McMichael finished it. Carcone had a night either way: six shots on goal in 13 and a half minutes and nothing past Hofer until the skills contest.

For the Mammoth, a point is a point, but they are now winless in four (0-2-2), and they are doing it shorthanded: Daily Faceoff reported Dylan Guenther is out two to four weeks with an upper-body injury. A team that can't score on 29 shots and four power plays will feel that absence.
headline: Sixteen shooters, no goals, and Hofer wins it
